about: Hand-entered table of historical cities with population estimates over time, used to place and size settlements on the globe for any date from the Neolithic to today. Years are integers: negative = BC as written (-3700 is 3700 BC), positive = AD, and there is no year 0. "founded" is the approximate start of settlement of urban character; "end", when present, is when the place was abandoned or ceased to be a city (omitted for cities that still exist). "styles" lists [fromYear, style] architectural eras, each valid until the next entry; "pop" lists [year, population] points to interpolate between; "names" (optional) lists [fromYear, name] for renamed cities. Pre-1950 figures follow Chandler (1987) "Four Thousand Years of Urban Growth", Modelski (2003) "World Cities -3000 to 2000", Morris (2010) and Bairoch (1988), supplemented by archaeological estimates for prehistoric, Bronze Age and pre-Columbian sites and by national censuses; 1950, 2000 and 2020 values for living cities are urban-agglomeration (metro) populations from UN World Urbanization Prospects 2018 where listed, otherwise city or municipality figures. All values are approximate: ancient and medieval populations are often uncertain by a factor of two or more, founding and end dates are rounded, and the positions of a few unlocated sites (notably Akkad) are conjectural.
